examples.title: Expressions & dynamic values
examples.about: Floor division, true division, big ints, f-strings, comparison chains.
examples.code:
# Basic: dynamic values, operator precedence, Python's floor division and
# modulo, true division, unbounded-looking integers and string operations.
WIDTH = 12
HEIGHT = 5

a, b = 7, 3
result = a + b * 2
grouped = (a + b) * 2
area = WIDTH * HEIGHT
unused = area * 100
ratio = area / (2 * (WIDTH + HEIGHT))
print("result =", result, "grouped =", grouped)
print("area =", area, "ratio =", ratio)
print("-17 // 5 =", -17 // 5, " -17 % 5 =", -17 % 5)     # floor semantics
print("2 ** 62 =", 2 ** 62, " 7 / 2 =", 7 / 2)
name = "compiler"
print(name.upper(), len(name), name[0] + name[-1], name * 2)
print(f"{area:>6} | {ratio:.3f} | {name!r}")
print(1 < 2 < 3, 3 > 2 > 2, "pi" in "pipeline", None is None)

examples.title: Optimization showcase
examples.about: Only proven integers are rewritten; unknown types are left alone.
examples.code:
# Optimization showcase for Python. Values are dynamically typed, so the
# optimizer only rewrites an operation when it can prove the operands are
# plain ints (e.g. a loop counter from range()); "x * 1" on an unknown x is
# kept, because x could be an object with its own __mul__.


def folding():
    seconds = 60 * 60 * 24
    weeks = seconds * 7
    return weeks // 3600


def propagation(n):
    scale = 4
    offset = scale * 2 + 1
    total = 0
    for i in range(n):
        total += i * scale + offset
    return total


def proven_ints(n):
    acc = 0
    for i in range(n):
        doubled = i * 2          # i is a proven int: strength-reduced to i + i
        same = doubled + 0       # and simplified
        acc += same
    return acc


def unknown_types(x):
    a = x * 1                    # kept: x might be a str, a list or an object
    return a


def dead_code(x):
    debug = False
    unused = x * 37
    if debug:
        print("debug", x)
    return x + 1


print("folding =", folding())
print("propagation =", propagation(10))
print("proven ints =", proven_ints(10))
print("unknown types =", unknown_types(21), unknown_types("ab"))
print("dead code =", dead_code(41))

lexical.title: Custom rules: calculator
lexical.about: A rule set written from scratch: lexical analysis and automata only.
lexical.code:
-- area of a ring
let outer := 12.5
let inner := 4
let area := 3.14159 * (outer ^ 2 - inner ^ 2)
print area / 2
lexical.rulesText:
# A small custom rule set: a calculator language with variables.
# Lexical analysis only -- the parser grammar belongs to C, Java and Python,
# so these tokens are recognised and visualised but not parsed.
LET      1  token  let|print
FLOAT    2  token  [0-9]+\.[0-9]+
INT      2  token  [0-9]+
NAME     2  token  [a-z][a-z0-9]*
ASSIGN   2  token  :=
OP       2  token  [-+*/^]
PAREN    2  token  [()]
COMMENT  2  skip   --[^\n]*
WS       3  skip   [ \t\r\n]+

defaultRules.C:
# Token rules for C.   Usage: ./lexer program.c --rules rules/c.rules
#
# One rule per line:  NAME  PRIORITY  token|skip  REGEX
#   PRIORITY  breaks ties when two rules match the same length (lower wins)
#   skip      the match is consumed but not emitted (whitespace, comments)
# In REGEX, \n \t \r \f \v are those characters; any other \x is a literal x.

KEYWORD    1  token  auto|break|case|char|const|continue|default|do|double|else|enum|extern|float|for|goto|if|inline|int|long|register|restrict|return|short|signed|sizeof|static|struct|switch|typedef|union|unsigned|void|volatile|while|_Bool|_Complex|_Atomic|_Static_assert|_Noreturn|_Thread_local|_Alignas|_Alignof|_Generic
DIRECTIVE  1  token  #[ \t]*[a-z]+([^\n\\]|\\[^\n]|\\\n)*
COMMENT    2  skip   //[^\n]*|/\*([^*]|\*+[^*/])*\*+/
STRING     2  token  (L|u8|u|U)?"([^"\\\n]|\\[^\n])*"
CHAR       2  token  (L|u|U)?'([^'\\\n]|\\[^\n])+'
NUMBER     2  token  0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+[uUlL]*|[0-9]+[uUlL]*|[0-9]+\.[0-9]*([eE][+\-]?[0-9]+)?[fFlL]?|\.[0-9]+([eE][+\-]?[0-9]+)?[fFlL]?|[0-9]+[eE][+\-]?[0-9]+[fFlL]?
IDENT      2  token  [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*
OP         2  token  <<=|>>=|\.\.\.|->|\+\+|--|&&|\|\||==|!=|<=|>=|<<|>>|\+=|-=|\*=|/=|%=|&=|\|=|\^=|##|[-+*/%=<>!&|^~?#]
PUNCT      2  token  [(){}\[\];,.:]
WS         3  skip   [ \t\r\n\f\v]+
defaultRules.Java:
# Token rules for Java.   Usage: ./lexer Program.java --rules rules/java.rules
#
# One rule per line:  NAME  PRIORITY  token|skip  REGEX
#   PRIORITY  breaks ties when two rules match the same length (lower wins)
#   skip      the match is consumed but not emitted (whitespace, comments)
# In REGEX, \n \t \r \f \v are those characters; any other \x is a literal x.
#
# Differences from C: no preprocessor, '@' starts annotations, '>>>' and
# '>>>=' are unsigned shifts, text blocks use """...""", literals may contain
# '_' separators, and true/false/null are keywords.

KEYWORD    1  token  abstract|assert|boolean|break|byte|case|catch|char|class|const|continue|default|do|double|else|enum|extends|final|finally|float|for|goto|if|implements|import|instanceof|int|interface|long|native|new|package|private|protected|public|return|short|static|strictfp|super|switch|synchronized|this|throw|throws|transient|try|void|volatile|while|true|false|null|var|record
COMMENT    2  skip   //[^\n]*|/\*([^*]|\*+[^*/])*\*+/
STRING     2  token  """([^"\\]|\\[^\n]|\\\n|"[^"]|""[^"])*"""|"([^"\\\n]|\\[^\n])*"
CHAR       2  token  '([^'\\\n]|\\[^\n]|\\u[0-9a-fA-F]+)'
NUMBER     2  token  0[xX][0-9a-fA-F_]+[lL]?|0[bB][01_]+[lL]?|[0-9][0-9_]*[lLfFdD]?|[0-9][0-9_]*\.[0-9_]*([eE][+\-]?[0-9]+)?[fFdD]?|\.[0-9][0-9_]*([eE][+\-]?[0-9]+)?[fFdD]?|[0-9][0-9_]*[eE][+\-]?[0-9]+[fFdD]?
IDENT      2  token  [a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*
OP         2  token  >>>=|<<=|>>=|>>>|\.\.\.|->|::|\+\+|--|&&|\|\||==|!=|<=|>=|<<|>>|\+=|-=|\*=|/=|%=|&=|\|=|\^=|[-+*/%=<>!&|^~?@]
PUNCT      2  token  [(){}\[\];,.:]
WS         3  skip   [ \t\r\n\f\v]+
defaultRules.Python:
# Token rules for Python.   Usage: ./lexer program.py --rules rules/python.rules
#
# One rule per line:  NAME  PRIORITY  token|skip  REGEX
#   PRIORITY  breaks ties when two rules match the same length (lower wins)
#   skip      the match is consumed but not emitted (whitespace, comments)
# In REGEX, \n \t \r \f \v are those characters; any other \x is a literal x.
#
# Differences from C: '#' starts a comment, '//' is floor division, strings
# can be triple-quoted and carry r/b/f/u prefixes. Indentation is treated as
# plain whitespace (no INDENT/DEDENT tokens).

KEYWORD    1  token  False|None|True|and|as|assert|async|await|break|class|continue|def|del|elif|else|except|finally|for|from|global|if|import|in|is|lambda|nonlocal|not|or|pass|raise|return|try|while|with|yield|match|case|self
COMMENT    2  skip   #[^\n]*
STRING     2  token  [rRbBuUfF]*("""([^"\\]|\\[^\n]|\\\n|"[^"]|""[^"])*"""|'''([^'\\]|\\[^\n]|\\\n|'[^']|''[^'])*'''|"([^"\\\n]|\\[^\n])*"|'([^'\\\n]|\\[^\n])*')
NUMBER     2  token  0[xX][0-9a-fA-F_]+|0[bB][01_]+|0[oO][0-7_]+|[0-9][0-9_]*(\.[0-9_]*)?([eE][+\-]?[0-9]+)?[jJ]?|\.[0-9]+([eE][+\-]?[0-9]+)?[jJ]?
IDENT      2  token  [a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*
OP         2  token  \*\*=|//=|>>=|<<=|->|:=|\*\*|//|==|!=|<=|>=|<<|>>|\+=|-=|\*=|/=|%=|&=|\|=|\^=|@=|[-+*/%=<>!&|^~@]
PUNCT      2  token  [(){}\[\];,.:]
WS         3  skip   [ \t\r\n\f\v\\]+
